IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/SPECIAL CIVIL APPLICATION NO. 6890 of 2025  ==========================================================
 IQBALBHAI USMANBHAI VAHORA  Versus  THE REGIONAL PASSPORT OFFICE  ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR RISHABH R JAIN(12326) for the Petitioner(s) No. 1  ==========================================================

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANIRUDDHA P. MAYEE
The learned counsel Mr. Kshitij Amin waives service of notice on behalf of the respondent.
2. Heard learned Counsels for the parties.
3. It is submitted that the petitioner has applied for Passport since all the pages of the petitioner's passport in possession has got exhausted and filled up.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has applied for reissue of fresh passport.
Learned Counsel submits that the petitioner was thereafter given an appointment.
However, the petitioner was informed that the petitioner shall have to take a NOC from the Court where the criminal case against the petitioner is pending.

Learned Counsel submits that the criminal proceedings which are pending against the petitioner are under Section 498A of the IPC, where the petitioner has appeared and there is no order for depositing of the passport or for any injunction to travel abroad.
Learned Counsel submits that the respondents are not processing the application of the petitioner in the said background.

sentences.text:
Learned Counsel Mr. Kshitij Amin submits that now in view of the Notification dated 18.02.2025,
the application of the petitioner shall be processed as per the provisions of GSR 570(E) dated 25.08.1993.

5. Considering the above submissions and the fact that there is no prohibition for the petitioner to travel abroad or any similar condition imposed by the Court in the proceedings under Section 498A,
the respondent is directed to process the application of the petitioner for a period of five years within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
6. With the aforesaid direction, the Special Civil Application stands disposed of.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
